findings.claim: Chart-switching geodesic integration is ready for tool paths over physical parts

hypothesis: An atlas of charts with exact transitions through the embedding integrates geodesics through or near a chart's coordinate singularity with an accuracy that does not depend on how close they pass, while a single chart loses accuracy or fails near its singular point. Shown for the two-chart polar atlas of the sphere (great circles through and near a pole) and for the Monge-plus-polar atlas of the Gaussian bump built from a ChartMap (geodesics through and near the apex).
input_data: unit sphere; great circles with closest approach delta in [0.0, 0.1, 0.01, 0.001, 0.0001, 1e-06, 1e-08, 1e-10, 1e-12] to the north pole, azimuth 1.3, full length 2 pi

meridian (delta = 0) in chart A alone from the declared angular-momentum seed L0 = sin^2(theta0) v_phi0 = 1e-12 at 101 step counts (350..450); at the other half-decade seeds from 1e-15 to 1e-10 the step counts whose closest RK4 stage point lies within 2 d* of a pole; 400 steps also at L0 / 10; unseeded at 400 steps
256 + 4096 seeded sphere points for transitions and covering (seed 3337)

Gaussian bump h = 0.5, sigma = 1: geodesics from x = -1.5 at offset delta in [0.0, 0.1, 0.01, 0.001, 0.0001, 1e-06, 1e-08] from the apex, length 3.0, RK4 200 steps, reference Monge chart alone at 800 steps; 256 seeded points of the Monge disc of radius 2.0 (seed 3661)
interface under test: ciw.lab.surfaces and ciw.lab.integrators at the source digests recorded in provider_runtime_identity.sources
mathematical_model: Atlas: charts X_c with closed-form inverses; u_B = X_B^{-1}(X_A(u_A)), v_B = g_B^{-1} J_B^T J_A v_A; regularity lambda_min / lambda_max of g (scale free); switch between RK4 steps when the active chart's regularity < 1/4. Sphere: chart A X = R(sin t cos p, sin t sin p, cos t), chart B = R_y(pi/2) X_A; regularity sin^2 theta = det g / R^4 in each chart and sin^2 theta_A + sin^2 theta_B = 1 + y^2/R^2 >= 1, so the better chart always has regularity >= 1/2. Meridian in chart A: angular momentum L = sin^2(theta) v_phi (0 on the meridian, sin(delta) on a unit-speed great circle passing delta from the pole) starts at a declared seed L0; near a pole the chart is the plane's polar chart, so the outcome depends on d/h and L0/h only (d the closest RK4 stage point's distance to the pole); a crossing multiplies L by a factor proportional to (h/d)^2 and turns nonlinear once L h^2/d^3 reaches order 1, so two crossings fail within about d* = (L0 h^4)^(1/5) (exponent from this argument, constant fitted). Graph z = f(x, y): Monge chart g = I + grad f grad f^T with regularity 1/(1 + |grad f|^2), and the polar chart (r, t) pulled back through PolarChart, singular at r = 0.
numerical_result: sphere atlas through the pole: error 4.86e-08, 4 switches (A->B, B->A, A->B, B->A); atlas error spread over delta 1.21x; orders 4.16, 3.96; single chart failed for 4 and degraded (>10x atlas) for 7 of 8 delta > 0; meridian in chart A alone from the seed 1e-12: 400-step error 1.03e-07 (10 times the error from a seed of 1e-13 is 1.03e-07), the two crossings amplifying L to 1.03e-07; over 101 step counts 5 runs have an RK4 stage point within d* of a pole and 5 fail, the largest d/d* of a failure 0.605 and the smallest of any other run 1.81; the runs beyond d* err 6.4e-08 to 0.057; across 11 seeds from 1e-15 to 1e-10 (188 runs, 64 failures) the largest d/d* of a failure is 1.41 and the smallest of a run that did not fail 0.988; unseeded, g_12 = 1.47e-17 and v_phi = 0 at the start and |L| <= 7.64e-19 before the first crossing, amplified to 7.35e-14 with error 7.42e-14 at 400 steps; transitions round trip 6.5e-16, speed 5.25e-16, Jacobian 3.72e-10; covering bound 0.502. Gaussian-bump atlas: error <= 4.05e-09 for every delta (Monge chart alone 6.11e-11), polar chart alone failed for 2 and degraded for 6 of 6 delta > 0; transitions round trip 6e-16, speed 8.17e-16, Jacobian 3.02e-10.
observation_model: Ambient error max_s |X_num(s) - X_ref(s)|: exact great circle cos(s) X0 + sin(s) T0 on the sphere, the refined Monge-chart run on the bump.

title: Add chart-transition support.
uncertainty: Atlas errors are RK4 truncation errors (order 4); the 400-step sphere error differs from the fourth-order predictions of the 200- and 800-step runs by 11.7%. Single-chart errors for small delta come from the unresolved azimuthal rate 1/sin(delta) at a fixed step; the failure steps and the errors for delta <= 1e-8 depend on rounding and may differ across platforms. On the meridian the single-chart result depends on the step grid and on the angular momentum L = sin^2(theta) v_phi that each pole crossing amplifies, so the 400-step success is a property of that grid (closest RK4 stage point 0.00254 from a pole) and of the seed, not of the chart. Unseeded, L comes from the rounding of g_12, which depends on the BLAS kernel (the BLAS build and the inputs of the OpenBLAS kernel choice are recorded in the runtime identity and in meridian-steps.json), so the meridian runs from a declared seed of 1e-12: the natural seed is at most 1e-16, 0.0001 of the declared one. It moves an error linear in the seed (the 400-step grid) by at most 0.0001 relative, an error quadratic in it (grids within a few d*, where perturbing the seed gave exponents up to 2.01) by at most about 0.0002, and the 400-step error from a seed of 1e-13 by at most 0.001; that error differs from proportionality by 1.73e-06. At the smallest swept seeds the bound is a larger share (up to 0.1 at 1e-15), so of the swept runs only the outcomes are compared. The failure radius d* takes its exponent from the scaling argument and its constant 1 from a fit; across the seed sweep the largest d/d* of a failure is 1.41 and the smallest of a run that did not fail 0.988.
unresolved_assumptions: An atlas needs an embedding and a closed-form inverse for each chart; atlases are built here for the sphere (rotated polar charts) and for graph surfaces (Monge chart and its polar ChartMap); intrinsic charts such as the hyperbolic plane are not covered.
Switching happens between steps; an adaptive integrator would need event location at the threshold.
The recorded minimum regularity of the active chart restates the switch threshold and the covering bound; it is reported, not checked.

The failure radius d* = (L0 h^4)^(1/5) takes its exponent from the scaling argument and its constant 1 from a fit. It is checked on one path at half-decade seeds from 1e-15 to 1e-10, beyond 2 d* at the declared seed only; finer seed steps or other paths may widen the band of d/d* in which failed and completed runs overlap. Near d* a run that does not fail can still err by order 1.
